idea-plugin.name: Invariant
idea-plugin.description:
Invariant is a semantic dark editor color scheme based on Monokai.

Color identifies what a symbol is; formatting shows how it is being used. Common code stays relatively quiet, while types, parameters, methods, reserved names, annotations, and comments remain easy to find.

The scheme provides explicit coverage for Java, Kotlin, Python, CSS, and shell scripts, with Language Defaults for other supported languages.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Corrects colors that never reached the editor, and adds Markdown styling.

  • Class references, reserved names, Python self and cls, and Kotlin operator and dynamic-call punctuation now render their intended colors. They previously fell back to whichever color the IDE declares for them.
  • Type parameters use a bold orange rather than a muted rose.
  • Markdown emphasis and headings carry structure through weight, on the identifier foreground.
  • Python byte strings follow the ordinary string color.
  • Python special names are green where they are defined and neutral where they are read, matching the other editors.
